packageRules.description: One branch per run for every non-major update, in every ecosystem. Omitting matchManagers is deliberate: the managers matcher imposes no constraint when it is absent, so this covers gomod, npm, cargo, pep621, swift, terraform, helm and the rest without enumeration

Digest and pin moves keep the tag, so they are a rebuilt layer rather than an upgrade decision and belong in one branch of their own. They are a separate rule because the non-major group above matches only minor and patch

A pre-1.0 package may break on a minor and semver permits it, so it leaves the automerging group into one of its own. WARNING: it must leave rather than merely lose automerge, because a branch automerges only when every upgrade in it does, so a single pre-1.0 member would park the whole group
A major upgrade is a decision, not a refresh, so it waits to be asked for on the dashboard
Anything that will merge itself says so on the pull request. Minor is qualified because the pre-1.0 rule above withholds automerge from it
